title: Curated reference bundles & access flow for config-triggered evals
creator: Maya Lin
description:
Problem: Model/config rollouts occasionally cause subtle quality regressions that are only discovered in production or via ad-hoc evals. Current promptset/golden dataset workflows are fragmented: curators store artifacts in disparate locations, access controls are manual, and there is no lightweight versioned bundle that maps directly to a config change.

Goal: Define and deliver a first-class artifact type called 'reference bundle' (RB) that bundles a curated prompt/ground-truth set, scoring scripts, and metadata (owner, version, checksum, allowed-rollout-tags). Provide curation guidelines, RB access/approval flows, signed immutable snapshots, and CI integrations so any config/model change can trigger targeted evals against relevant RBs before rollout.

Scope:
- Create RB schema and storage conventions (immutable snapshots with signer metadata).
- RB curation guide and steward role definition.
- ACL model and lightweight approval flows (curator -> steward -> security for sensitive RBs).
- CI/console integration: map config keys to RBs, run evals on PRs/rollouts, surface metrics and regression gates in Console.

Out of scope: automated dataset generation, full policy engine for lifetime of RBs (follow-ups will cover retention/expiry automation).
acceptance_criteria: A1: RB JSON schema defined and documented in Confluence with required metadata fields (owner, steward, version, checksum, tags, allowed-rollback-strategy).
A2: Storage path and immutability guarantee implemented for RB snapshots (S3 prefix + signed manifest).
A3: RB creation flow in Console: curator can create draft RB, assign steward, attach approval checklist, and mark snapshot as signed.
A4: Minimal RB ACL model: RBs can be marked public/internal/secret and mapped to user groups; access enforced in RB store.
A5: CI integration: config/model PRs can declare affected RB keys; PR pipeline runs evals against declared RBs and fails if any configured metric regresses beyond thresholds.
A6: Console shows per-RB historical eval runs with metrics and per-metric trendline and links to the triggering PR/rollout.
A7: Curation guide and steward runbook published and approved by product, infra, and security.

decisions: D1: Use 'reference bundle' (RB) term instead of 'golden dataset' to emphasize scope (prompts + scoring + metadata) and avoid 'immutable canonical' connotations.

D2: Signed manifest approach chosen over object-level immutability to allow storage cost optimizations while preserving snapshot integrity via checksum+signature. Signature keys will be held by curator role with steward co-sign for high-risk RBs.
D3: RB ACL model will reuse existing org groups and the Console's RB creation UX will default to 'internal' to avoid accidental public exposure.
D4: CI gating uses configurable per-RB thresholds (absolute and relative) and a 'soft-fail' mode for early visibility without blocking for first 2 cycles.
tradeoffs: T/O1: Strict immutability would simplify provenance but increase storage duplication; chosen signed-manifest minimizes duplication at cost of a slightly more complex verification step.
T/O2: Per-RB complex ACLs give fine-grained security but add operational overhead; we start with 3 visibility modes (public/internal/secret) and iterate.
T/O3: Blocking CI on first-run regressions reduces release risk but increases rollbacks and alert noise; initial rollout will use soft-fail for 2 cycles as data is gathered.
